tasks.title: Expose a typed plugin manifest
tasks.objective: Let hosts register provider, skill, and command contributions through one host-neutral Core contract.
tasks.outcome: Plugins can be validated, listed, and activated without editor/vendor branches or duplicate Runtime state.
acceptance: The manifest type is exported from Core and validates IDs, versions, and optional contributions.
The registry rejects duplicate plugin/provider IDs and exposes a deterministic catalog to the host.
A production caller uses the contract to build the default provider catalog; mutation of registration makes the focused test fail.

verification.proves: Plugin API is connected to production code

tasks.title: Document durable Agent and Workspace naming
tasks.objective: Teach the Agent Skill how to choose readable self and workspace display names without changing stable IDs or paths.
tasks.outcome: The generated Skill contains both naming workflows, constraints, and failure behavior.
acceptance: Skill text describes naming the current Agent and the containing Workspace separately.
Skill text states that display names persist while Session/Workspace IDs and paths remain stable, and it names the user-visible recovery path on failure.
The focused help test proves both naming instructions are present and fails when either is removed.
